verifiedFacts: Both binaries: the default fetch after the remote branch's deletion prints 'Abandoned 1 commits' and leaves the workspace stale (jj status exit 1); with the key set false before the fetch, only 'legion/X@origin [deleted] untracked' prints, jj status exits 0, the pushed commit stays beneath @, the file stays on disk, the bookmark is gone.

jj config set --repo <key> false -R <clone>: exit 0, silent, idempotent, records no operation, snapshots nothing, merges into an existing per-repo file (the bot's user.* survive); the value must be the bare TOML boolean.

jj config path --repo -R <clone> is ~/.config/jj/repos/<config-id>/config.toml (the id from <clone>/.jj/repo/config-id), not inside the clone; workspaces share it through their .jj/repo pointer; jj config get prints false with -R <clone>, -R <workspace>, and cwd=workspace; under another HOME it prints true with 'Per-repo config not found'.
The production clone's per-repo file (config-id 834789e1326b209850cb) holds only the implementer bot's user.name/user.email today; no git.* key.
The per-repo write is in place (inode unchanged), not a rename.
jj op log --op-diff for the fetch shows Changed commits and Changed working copy sections only in the default case; with the setting only the two bookmark sections remain — the quotable window.
Baseline: packages/workspace 21 pass / 0 fail (28.8 s); CI runs packages/workspace lint/typecheck/test on jj 0.44.0; the workspace has no node_modules (bun install --frozen-lockfile before bunx tsc).
concerns: The setting lives in the daemon user's ~/.config/jj/repos/<config-id>/config.toml, not in the clone: the spec's 'the clone's jj repository settings' is imprecise; panes see it only because HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME are allow-listed and panes run as the daemon's user; the Kubernetes worker image (LEGION-24) needs the same HOME or its own write.

The per-repo write is in place, not atomic: a concurrent jj process reading in the microsecond window sees an empty or partial file once; expected rate far below one per year. Plan keeps the spec's unconditional write; a read-then-write-only-if-not-false variant is a one-branch change if the architect prefers it.

The live proof deletes the pushed sandbox branch with the Git refs API instead of merging: the gh shim refuses pr merge and any …/merge path for every worker role, and the ref deletion is what jj reacts to. Two inferences to confirm on the day: the implementer's own grant (implement App, account-wide install, token minted without repositories narrowing) can push to and delete a ref on sjawhar/legion-smoke; fallback is prompting the rig's architect over its shim socket, last resort the operator.

The rig is the full smoke rig in envoy mode against the shared LEGSMOKE project and cannot run beside a sibling tree's envoy rig; the resume is forced by killing the rig's own architect pane (a Dispatch comment on the rig issue makes the probe immediate).

The pane guard refuses any bash command mentioning jj with abandon/undo/restore/revert — the key's name included — so the implementer edits with edit/write, pipes the handoff JSON on stdin, uses --body-file, and keeps commit subjects free of those words (the plan's subjects are).
Every real-jj test leaves a ~/.config/jj/repos/<id>/config.toml on the developer box; jj already creates an empty one per scratch repo, so this is not new in kind.
